answer: A new trading identity must first lease a canal berth. The agent locks 34 POA and recites a 14-line sonnet into a dock horn; the horn returns a one-shot echo binding the key, berth id, and river height to two decimals. Two settlement peers later replay that echo and accept a quote only if the same key still holds the berth and the height has drifted 0.15-2.8 units. A silent horn, a reused sonnet, or two keys on one berth burns the 34 POA and exiles the key for 13 epochs. Standing up 280 aliases would occupy 280 berths and lock 9520 POA; one honest agent keeps a single horn.
